title: Examination of 2D Frontal and Sagittal Markerless Motion Capture: Implications for Markerless Applications
metricDefinition: OpenPose-derived 2D joint centers and joint angles are compared with reprojected marker-based results in frontal and sagittal views.

extractionLocations.description: Camera views, OpenPose keypoints, tracking, filtering, and joint-angle construction.
Agreement results by plane and visibility.
Occlusion, camera-side, and frontal-plane measurement limitations.

study.deviceAndEnvironment: Frontal and sagittal laboratory walking capture

measurements.definition: Markerless joint centers and biomechanical joint angles compared with reprojected marker-based reference data.
measurements.calculationMethod: Repeated-measures agreement analysis across walking trials.
notes: Biomechanical joint angles are not a left-right shoulder-line angle.

reportedFindings.summary: Visibility, occlusion, view plane, and anatomical labeling affect 2D markerless agreement.

faceFitMappings.paperMetricName: biomechanical shoulder joint center and joint angles
faceFitMappings.reason: Biomechanical joint-angle agreement is not baseline-relative left-right shoulder-line tilt.

thresholdAssessment.reason: Agreement and error values describe measurement validity, not seated interview behavior.

limitations: Walking and lower-body biomechanics do not transfer to seated upper-body scoring.
Occlusion and camera-plane effects require Face-Fit-specific validation.
